title: Adaptive kernel routing and clock policy for mixed MIG deployments
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Background: We see tail latency and cost variability for multi-tenant deployments on H100 and L40S when using mixed MIG slice sizes (e.g., 1g/2g/4g) and during workload phases that switch between long prefill and short decode bursts. Current kernel selection is static by model/shard and the scheduler applies a single GPU clock policy per node. This ticket prototypes an adaptive approach that picks kernel variants and per-MIG clock targets based on runtime signals (active KV cache hit rate, sequence length distribution, batch depth) and a lightweight cost/latency utility function. Goals: (1) reduce 95th/99th latency across mixed MIG slices by dynamically choosing attention kernel variants and adjusting GPU clocks within thermal/power constraints; (2) keep token cost neutral or improved for common workloads; (3) maintain stability during rapid prefill->decode transitions.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile token generation latency reduced by >= 15% for mixed MIG experiments vs baseline static kernel+clock config
Median cost-per-token does not increase by more than 5% for benchmark workloads
No CPU or GPU watchdog alerts triggered in 48h soak on canary fleet (stability check)
Automatic fallback to safe kernel/clock config if memory fragmentation or thermal headroom is below threshold
Feature flag and observability: kernel variant + clock policy traces are emitted per-request and visualized in Console dashboard (route-level)
implementation_plan: Instrument runtime to expose signals: KV cache hit ratio, active sequence length histogram, batch size distribution, MIG slice type on request path
Add kernel registry with metadata (expected decode/prefill efficiency by seq-len, preferred clock range)
Implement lightweight policy engine in runtime control plane: evaluate per-request utility and output kernel variant + clock target; run in fast-path with caching for route/model combos
Integrate with node agent to set per-MIG clock targets where supported (NVML/XNVML shim) and enforce safety hysteresis
Experiment harness: run A/B on staging fleet with traffic replay for 24h, collect latency/cost/thermal metrics
Iterate and harden fallbacks and rollout flags (canary -> 5% -> 25% -> global)
experiments: Staging experiment 2025-02-20: H100 80 nodes mixed 1g/2g/4g MIG slices. Adaptive policy chosen kernels K_attn_small/K_attn_prefill. Observed 18% reduction in p95 for a 1k-seqlen prefill-heavy workload.
L40S run 2025-02-26: baseline vs adaptive clocking with conservative cap. p99 improved by 12% on chat-like decode workloads with bursts; cost per token improved 3% due to fewer forced re-kernels.

A10 microbenchmarks: limited thermal headroom; adaptive policy fell back to low-clock kernels and showed no CPU-side contention but no meaningful latency wins; flagged for exclusion from aggressive clock changes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Aggressive clock changes may cause thermal spikes or preemption on shared tenants. Mitigation: enforce per-node cooling hysteresis and cap duty-cycle of clock adjustments.

Risk: Kernel mismatches cause correctness regressions for newer fused-attention kernels. Mitigation: kernel registry includes compatibility flags and QA tests; kernel selection always validated on a small dry-run path before global enablement.

Risk: NVML/driver differences across L40S/A10 variants. Mitigation: detect driver capabilities at node startup and maintain a per-node capability profile; include nodes in experiment only if shim returns success for clock ops.
notes: Design decision 2025-02-18: avoid per-request NVML calls — use node agent with an in-memory command queue to coalesce clock changes
Trade-off: per-route optimal kernels increase complexity in model onboarding; we will seed defaults and surface recommendations in Console Optimize.
Related work: follow-up ticket planned to extend policy to dedicated reserved pools (ENG-12510).
